title: MakeMyTrip's India Arm Wins Sebi Nod for IPO Built as Share Sale by Parent
excerpt: Sebi issued final observations on November 6 on the confidential July filing. The offer is a sale of MMT India shares by MakeMyTrip and ibibo Group Holdings, and the India unit stays a subsidiary after listing.
body:
• MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd has received Sebi's final observations, issued on November 6, clearing the way for its proposed initial public offering, according to an update on the regulator's website.
  • The IPO is structured as a sale of MMT India shares by its parent, Nasdaq-listed MakeMyTrip, and its wholly-owned subsidiary ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore) Pte Ltd — not a fresh issue of capital for the India business.
  • MMT India will remain a MakeMyTrip subsidiary after listing, with its results still consolidated into the parent's accounts.
  • The parent swung to a net profit of $1.8 million in the September quarter, against a loss of $5.7 million a year earlier, on revenue of $235.2 million, up 11.2 per cent.

MakeMyTrip's India subsidiary has received the Securities and Exchange Board of India's approval to launch an initial public offering, according to an update on the markets regulator's website on Monday.

MakeMyTrip (India) Ltd, headquartered in Gurugram, had filed draft papers with Sebi in July through the confidential route. After examining the draft documents, the regulator issued its final observations on November 6, PTI reported via The Hindu BusinessLine. Sebi's observations are the step that allows a company to proceed with preparations for a public issue, subject to applicable regulatory requirements.

How the issue is structured

The proposed IPO is expected to comprise a sale of equity shares in MMT India by its parent MakeMyTrip and by ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore) Pte Ltd, the parent said in a regulatory filing with Nasdaq. That structure matters for investors reading the offer: the money raised goes to the selling shareholders, not onto MMT India's balance sheet. The net proceeds received by MakeMyTrip and ibibo Group Holdings are expected to strengthen the parent's cash position and be used for long-term growth, strategic inorganic initiatives and repurchases of classes of its securities, including convertible securities, the filing stated.

Following the IPO, MMT India will continue to remain a subsidiary of MakeMyTrip, with its financial results continuing to be consolidated with those of the parent. MakeMyTrip said the listing is expected to enhance MMT India's brand visibility and support its ability to incentivise and promote talent in a competitive technology recruitment market.

The numbers behind the filing

MakeMyTrip swung back into profit for the three months ending September 2026, boosted by increased bookings across all categories. It reported a net profit of $1.8 million for the second quarter of FY27, compared with a loss of $5.7 million in the same period a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter touched $235.2 million, an increase of 11.2 per cent over the same period of the previous fiscal.

What to watch next

Sebi's observations clear the regulatory gate; they do not set the issue's size, price band or opening date, none of which has been announced. Those details, in the updated prospectus, are what will determine how much of MMT India public investors are being offered and at what valuation — the figures to wait for before judging the deal.
